title: Fix the instructions
summary: Find the single incorrect instruction that makes a sorting robot fail.

scenario.briefing: A sorting robot places every can into the wrong bin. The steps are all present and the counts are right, so one instruction must be wrong.

objectives.description: Choose a replacement that fixes the cause.

hints: Compare what the robot does with where the bins actually are.
The arm reaches the correct bin only if it turns toward it.
The robot turns left, but the recycling bin is on the right.
The faulty instruction is turn left. Replace it with turn right.

misconceptions.description: Changing the scan step instead of the movement.
misconceptions.feedback: Rescanning repeats the same wrong placement. The evidence points to movement, not scanning.
If you change two things, you cannot tell which change fixed the behavior. Make one justified change, then verify.

sections.title: Debugging is evidence-driven
sections.body: A bug is a mismatch between expected and actual behavior. Good debugging narrows the fault with observations before changing code. Changing several things at once destroys the evidence about which change mattered.

sections.title: Fix the cause, verify the behavior
sections.body: The robot's wrong bin is a symptom. The cause is a movement instruction pointing away from the bin. After one repair, rerun the behavior and check the result.

vocabulary.definition: A defect that makes behavior differ from expectation.
Visible wrong behavior caused by a defect.
The condition that produces the symptom.

steps.title: Find the faulty instruction
steps.prompt: The recycling bin is to the robot's right. Choose the instruction that is wrong, then choose the smallest repair.

instructions.label: Lower the can into the bin

steps.explanation: The bin is on the right, so the robot must turn right. Walking farther or rescanning does not change direction.

steps.title: How do you know it is fixed?
steps.prompt: After changing one instruction, what is the best next step?

options.label: Assume it works because the change looks right
Run the sorting task again and check the bin and scan result
Change two more instructions to be safe
Ask an AI whether the instruction sounds correct

quiz.explanation: Running the actual behavior and checking its outcome is stronger evidence than appearance or opinion.

hints: What evidence would show the robot now reaches the bin?
Run the behavior, do not just read it.
Check both the physical destination and the scan result.
Rerun the task and inspect where the can ends up.

steps.title: Debugging practice
steps.prompt: Select every statement that describes careful debugging.

statements.label: Change one suspected cause at a time.
Use observations to narrow where the fault can be.
Rewrite the whole project at the first failure.
Treating a symptom as proof of the root cause is enough.

steps.explanation: Careful debugging isolates one cause, verifies a change, and keeps evidence of what happened.

accessibility.summary: Instructions are radio options and the repair list is a separate radio group. Results are text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Choose the faulty instruction and repair with normal radio controls.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each instruction is announced with its position. The feedback states whether the selected fault and repair match the evidence.
